section_heading: Chapter 1: Kalpana Siddhi - Indications and Exclusions for Shodhana
text: Indications for Shodhana (purificatory elimination): Patients with Bahudoshavastha (excessive morbid doshas), characterized by heaviness of body, chronic metabolic sluggishness, loss of appetite, recurrent dermatological disorders, chronic toxic accumulation (Amadosha), and high stamina. Contraindications for Shodhana: Individuals suffering from extreme debility (Durbala), extreme thirst (Trishna), hunger (Kshudha), acute fever (Nava Jwara), pregnancy (Garbhini), puerperium (Sutika), active hemorrhage (Raktapitta), pediatric age below 10 years, and geriatric age above 70 years, unless life-threatening poisoning or acute emergency mandates.

section_heading: Chapter 6: Vamana-Virechana Vyapad Siddhi - The Ten Complications of Emesis and Purgation
text: Ten major complications (Vyapad) of faulty Vamana and Virechana: 1. Adhmana (abdominal distension and tympanites), 2. Parikartika (sharp cutting anorectal pain or fissure), 3. Srava (profuse watery or mucous discharge), 4. Hrit-graha (precordial constriction or cardiac distress), 5. Gatra-graha (generalized body stiffness), 6. Jibhva-graha (tongue stiffness or retraction), 7. Upadruta / Vibandha (obstruction of flatus and feces), 8. Stambha (rigid muscular spasms), 9. Klama (severe exhaustion without physical exertion), and 10. Ayoga / Atiyoga (inadequate elimination or life-threatening hyper-evacuation).

section_heading: Chapter 6: Management of Ati-Virechana (Excessive Purgation and Hypovolemia)
text: Emergency clinical protocol for Ati-Virechana (hyper-purgation, dehydration, and vascular collapse): 1. Immediate cessation of purgative intake. 2. Administration of cold water sprinkling, cooling pastes of sandalwood (Chandana) and Ushira to alleviate burning sensation. 3. Administration of Pichha Basti (soothing medicated enema prepared with boiled milk, ghee, Mocharasa / Bombax ceiba gum, and fresh goat blood or decoctions of astringent barks). 4. Oral administration of rehydrating gruels: Dhanya-Nagara Peya (gruel processed with coriander and dry ginger) sweetened with sugar and honey. 5. If fainting (Murcha) or hypovolemic shock occurs, administer sweet cardiac stimulants and keep patient in Trendelenburg position.

section_heading: Chapter 6: Management of Parikartika (Cutting Anorectal Pain and Fissure)
text: Management of Parikartika (acute cutting anal pain, tenesmus, and fissure following aggressive purgation or enema): Caused by administration of sharp (Teekshna) purgatives in a patient with dry bowel (Ruksha Koshtha) and low pitta. Clinical protocol: 1. Avoid all spicy, sour, and astringent foods. 2. Warm hip baths (Avagaha Sweda) with lukewarm milk or Dashamoola decoction. 3. Topical application and rectal instillation of Yashtimadhu Ghrita (licorice ghee) or Shatadhouta Ghrita to promote mucosal healing. 4. Administration of gentle Anuvasana Basti with Yashtimadhu Taila. 5. Diet strictly limited to sweet unctuous milk gruels (Kshira Peya).

section_heading: Chapter 7: Basti Vyapad Siddhi - The Twelve Complications of Medicated Enemas
text: Twelve complications (Basti Vyapad) resulting from faulty administration of enemas: 1. Ayoga (retention of enema without cleansing), 2. Atiyoga (severe diarrhea and dehydration), 3. Klama (fatigue), 4. Adhmana (meteorism / gaseous distension), 5. Hikka (persistent hiccups), 6. Hrid-prapti (cardiac distress due to upward migration of liquid), 7. Urdhva-gamana (regurgitation of enema fluid through mouth or nose), 8. Pravahika (severe tenesmus with dysentery), 9. Shoola (colic), 10. Parikartika (anal laceration), 11. Parisrava (continuous involuntary leakage), and 12. Pravahika / rectal bleeding. Primary causes: incorrect nozzle (Netra Dosha), faulty bladder pressure (Putaka Dosha), wrong temperature, or wrong posture.

section_heading: Chapter 7: Emergency Management of Basti Fluid Regurgitation (Urdhva-gamana)
text: Emergency protocol for Urdhva-gamana (upward movement and regurgitation of enema fluid toward stomach or chest): 1. Immediately cease administration and place patient in sitting posture. 2. Spray cold water on the face and chest. 3. Induce gentle downward peristalsis by rubbing sole of feet and calves with salt-oil warm paste. 4. Administer strong carminative downward-directing decoctions (Anulomana) such as Triphala with warm water. 5. If patient exhibits airway compromise or vomiting of enema fluid, maintain airway clearance, aspirate oral secretions, and administer warm medicated smoke (Dhumapana) to clear tracheal spasm.

section_heading: Chapter 12: Uttara-Basti Siddhi - Procedural Safety and Complications of Urethral/Vaginal Enemas
text: Uttara Basti (intra-urethral and intra-uterine enema) safety guidelines: Strict asepsis is mandatory. Indications: infertility (Vandhyatva), severe dysmenorrhea (Kashta-artava), uterine prolapse, recurrent urinary retention (Mutraghata), and chronic bladder pain. Contraindications: acute urethritis, gonococcal or severe purulent discharge, cervical malignancy, active pelvic inflammatory crisis, and pregnancy. Maximum urethral dose for males: 1/2 Pala (approx 24 ml); for females: 1 Pala (approx 48 ml) for vaginal/uterine instillation. Complications: urinary tract infection, hematuria, acute pelvic colic. Management: urethral wash with lukewarm decoction of Gokshura and Nyagrodha barks; oral administration of Chandanasava.

section_heading: Chapter 13: Snehadhyaya - Absolute and Relative Contraindications for Internal Oleation (Snehapana)
text: Contraindications for internal oleation (Snehapana): Internal ghee/oil therapy must NEVER be administered to: 1. Patients with acute digestive impairment (Mandagni) or Ama accumulation, 2. Acute fever (Nava Jwara), 3. Severe liver enlargement with ascites (Jalodara), 4. Acute diarrhea (Atisara), 5. Morbid obesity (Ati-sthoulya), 6. Severe nausea or persistent vomiting (Chhardi), 7. Acute poisoning, 8. Alcohol intoxication (Madatyaya), and 9. Pregnancy in early trimesters. Administering Sneha in Ama condition leads to incurable systemic endotoxemia (Amadosha), dermatological obstinacy, and severe cardiometabolic collapse.

section_heading: Chapter 13: Snehadhyaya - Signs of Proper, Deficient, and Excessive Oleation (Samyak, Ayoga, Atiyoga)
text: Clinical criteria for assessing Snehana progress: Samyak Snigdha Lakshana (proper oleation): Vatanulomana (unobstructed downward passage of flatus and feces), Deeptagni (strong appetite), unctuous and loose stools (Snigdha Asamhata Pureesha), softness and unctuousness of skin (Snigdha Gatrata), and aversion to further fat intake (Sneha Udvega). Ayoga Lakshana (under-oleation): Dry hard stools, rough skin, burning digestion, and stiffness. Atiyoga Lakshana (excessive oleation): Pallor (Panduta), heaviness of body, indigestion, drowsiness, nausea, and presence of undigested fat in feces. Management of Atiyoga: fasting (Langhana), dry powders (Ruksha Churna), Triphala decoction, and Takra (buttermilk).

section_heading: Chapter 14: Swedadhyaya - Contraindications and Complications of Sudation (Swedana)
text: Contraindications for Sudation (Swedana Anarha): Swedana must not be administered in: 1. Hemorrhagic disorders (Raktapitta), 2. Severe Pitta constitution or aggravated Pitta, 3. Uncontrolled diabetes (Prameha), 4. Acute diarrhea and dysentery, 5. Severe emaciation (Kshina), 6. Cardiac disease (Hridroga), 7. Extreme dizziness (Bhrama), 8. Blindness or eye inflammation (Timira), 9. Pregnancy (Garbhini), and 10. Testicular and scrotal swelling. In cardiac, ocular, and testicular regions, only extremely mild or no heat may ever be applied. Complications of Atisveda (excessive sudation): fainting (Murcha), thermal burns, extreme thirst, joint flaccidity, and fever. Antidote: cooling baths, sugar water, sweet fruit juices, and application of sandalwood.

section_heading: Chapter 15: Upakalpaniya Adhyaya - Panchakarma Clinic Infrastructure and Emergency Readiness
text: Mandatory clinical infrastructure and emergency readiness for a Panchakarma theater (Upakalpaniya provisions): The clinic must be well-ventilated, protected from strong drafts, noise, and odors. Essential emergency supplies: Clean water storage, heating vessels, Dronis (massage and enema tables of standardized dimensions), graduated measuring vessels, and soft sterile dressings. Emergency medicine cabinet must stock: Lifesaving antidotes for hyper-evacuation, anti-emetic powders (Mayurapiccha Bhasma, Eladi Churna), cardiac stimulants (Kasturi, Shringabhasma), digestive restoratives (Trikatu, Hingwashtaka, Chitrakadi Vati), hemostatic powders (Lodhra, Nagakeshara), ghee, honey, milk, rock salt (Saindhava), and fresh goat milk. Trained nursing personnel must monitor patient pulse, respirations, and mental orientation throughout procedures.

section_heading: Section 3: Standard Operating Protocol for Vamana Karma (Therapeutic Emesis)
text: Standard Operating Protocol for Vamana Karma: Pre-procedure (Purva Karma): Internal oleation (Snehapana) with medicated ghee (e.g., Indukanta Ghrita or Mahatiktaka Ghrita) in escalating doses for 3 to 7 days until Samyak Snigdha signs appear, followed by one day of resting diet (Kapha-aggravating meals like curd and black gram) and Abhyanga-Swedana. Procedure day (Pradhana Karma): Confirm morning fasting state. Administer stomach-filling liquid (Akantha-pana) using milk, sugarcane juice, or Yashtimadhu Phanta. Administer Vamana Yoga (Madanaphala Pippali churna 3-6g with Vacha, honey, and Saindhava). Observe Vega (emetic bouts) count: Pravara (8 Vegas), Madhyama (6 Vegas), Avara (4 Vegas). Target termination: Appearance of Pittanta (yellowish bile in vomitus), lightness of chest, and cessation of emetic urge.

section_heading: Section 4: Standard Operating Protocol for Virechana Karma (Therapeutic Purgation)
text: Standard Operating Protocol for Virechana Karma: Indications: Chronic skin disorders (Eczema, Psoriasis), Liver disorders (Jaundice, Hepatitis), Chronic fever, Gouty arthritis (Vatarakta), Chronic hyperacidity (Amlapitta), and Bronchial asthma with Pitta involvement. Pre-procedure: 3-7 days Snehapana, 3 days Sarvanga Abhyanga and Bashpa Sweda, light dinner previous night. Procedure day: Administer Virechana formulation between 9:00 AM and 10:00 AM (after Kapha time subsides). Formulations: Trivrit Leham (15-30g), Ichhabhedi Rasa (125-250mg for severe constipation only), or Castor oil with ginger water. Vega counting: Pravara (30 stools), Madhyama (20 stools), Avara (10 stools). Target end-point: Kaphanta (mucus appearing in final bowel movements), relief of abdomen, normal vital signs.

section_heading: Section 5: Post-Shodhana Graduated Dietary Regimen (Samsarjana Krama)
text: Post-purificatory dietary schedule (Samsarjana Krama) to reignite sluggish digestive fire (Mandagni): 1. Peya (thin clear rice gruel without salt or spices): provides hydration and easy assimilation. 2. Vilepi (thick rice gruel): restores bodily vigor and peristalsis. 3. Akrita Yusha (unseasoned green gram / Mung lentil soup without salt and oil). 4. Krita Yusha (seasoned Mung soup cooked with mild ghee, cumin, and Saindhava salt). 5. Akrita Mamsa Rasa (unseasoned clear meat broth) followed by Krita Mamsa Rasa (seasoned broth) for non-vegetarians, or seasoned pulse soups for vegetarians. Dosing cycles based on Shuddhi grade: Pravara Shuddhi (3 meal sessions each stage, 7 days total); Madhyama Shuddhi (2 meal sessions each stage, 5 days total); Avara Shuddhi (1 meal session each stage, 3 days total). Strict prohibition: Heavy, cold, fried, curd, and sour foods are strictly forbidden during Samsarjana Krama.

section_heading: Section 6: Basti Administration Protocols - Niruha and Anuvasana
text: Clinical Protocols for Basti Administration: Kala Basti (16 enemas: 10 Anuvasana oil, 6 Niruha decoction); Karma Basti (30 enemas: 18 Anuvasana, 12 Niruha); Yoga Basti (8 enemas: 5 Anuvasana, 3 Niruha). Order of administration: Always commence and conclude with Anuvasana (unctuous oil enema) to protect rectal mucosa from Vata aggravation. Niruha Basti preparation order: 1. Makshika (honey) and Saindhava (rock salt) triturated thoroughly, 2. Sneha (medicated oil/ghee) added and emulsified, 3. Kalka (fine medicinal herbal paste) blended, 4. Kwatha (warm decoction) added gradually, and 5. Avapa (adjuvant liquids) mixed into homogenous emulsion. Patient positioning: Left lateral position (Vama Parshwa) with left leg extended and right leg flexed at hip and knee.

document_version: CCRAS 2008 Edition; Department of AYUSH, Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
section_heading: Chapter 2: Patient Screening and Informed Consent in Panchakarma
text: Mandatory clinical screening criteria before commencing any Panchakarma procedure: 1. Comprehensive baseline physical examination including recording of Blood Pressure, Resting Heart Rate, Respiratory Rate, Blood Glucose (RBS), ECG for patients above 45 years, and routine urinalysis. 2. Detailed Prakriti and Vikriti assessment to identify doshic predisposition and tolerance thresholds. 3. Verification of patient's current Western pharmacological regimen (e.g., anti-hypertensives, anticoagulants, antiplatelets, insulin, oral hypoglycemics). Patients on Warfarin, Heparin, or Clopidogrel must NOT undergo Raktamokshana or invasive Siravyadha without hematologist clearance. 4. Execution of written informed consent documenting procedure steps, dietary limitations, and recognized potential side effects.

section_heading: Chapter 5: Operational Safety and Infection Control in Jalaukavacharana (Leech Therapy)
text: Operational safety guidelines for Jalaukavacharana (Leech Therapy): 1. Leech selection: Only certified non-poisonous medicinal leeches (Hirudo medicinalis / Nirvisha Jalauka, recognized by green-brown dorsal stripes and active swimming motility) must be used. Never use wild uncertified leeches. 2. Single-patient use: A leech applied to a patient MUST be marked and quarantined or safely discarded according to biomedical waste rules. Never reuse a leech across different patients to eliminate hepatitis B, C, and HIV transmission risks. 3. Host preparation: Clean target skin thoroughly with sterile distilled water; avoid scented soaps, antiseptics, or alcohol immediately before application as leeches will refuse biting. 4. Post-detachment management: Leech is induced to vomit ingested blood using turmeric powder (Haridra Churna). Patient bite site is dusted with sterile Haridra or Shatadhouta Ghrita and sterile pressure dressing applied for 12 hours.

section_heading: Chapter 7: Prevention and Management of Scalds and Thermal Injuries during Swedana
text: Thermal safety protocol during Swedana (steam and bolus sudation): 1. Steam chamber (Bashpa Sweda) safety: Boiler pressure gauges must be calibrated quarterly. Steam temperature entering chamber must not exceed 42°C to 45°C. Patient's head must remain strictly outside the steam chamber with a cold wet towel wrapped on forehead. Continuous verbal communication with patient is mandatory; session terminated immediately upon profuse perspiration on forehead or patient request. Maximum duration: 15 to 20 minutes. 2. Pinda Sweda (Patra Pinda / Shashtika Shali Pinda Sweda): Therapist must test the bolus temperature on the dorsal aspect of their own wrist before touching patient skin. Never apply a boiling bolus directly. 3. First aid for thermal scald: Immediate application of cold water, Aloe vera pulp (Kumari Swarasa), or silver sulfadiazine ointment.

section_heading: Chapter 8: Emergency Management of Vasovagal Syncope and Hypotension in Panchakarma
text: Emergency Management of Vasovagal Syncope and Acute Hypotension during Panchakarma: Trigger factors: Orthostatic repositioning after steam bath, emotional fear during emesis, excessive bowel evacuation, or severe pain. Warning signs: Sudden pallor, cold clammy perspiration, yawning, dizziness, bradycardia, or dropping systolic BP below 90 mmHg. Immediate clinical action: 1. Terminate procedure instantly. 2. Place patient in supine position with legs elevated 30 degrees (Trendelenburg maneuver). 3. Loosen tight garments, ensure fresh airflow, administer high-flow oxygen via nasal cannula. 4. Spray cold water on face. 5. If conscious, administer lukewarm Draksha (raisin) water or glucose solution with a pinch of rock salt. 6. If unconsciousness persists beyond 60 seconds, initiate BLS resuscitation and emergency hospital transfer.

section_heading: Section 2: Adverse Drug Event (ADE) Monitoring during Snehapana and Shodhana
text: Pharmacovigilance monitoring for adverse drug reactions (ADR) during Panchakarma: Commonly observed adverse reactions: 1. Drug-induced gastritis and acute reflux from unrefined medicated ghees in high doses, 2. Severe electrolyte imbalance (hypokalemia and hyponatremia) secondary to uncontrolled emesis or purgation, 3. Allergic contact dermatitis from topical medicated oils (Taila) containing Bhallataka (Semecarpus anacardium) or Chitraka, 4. Anal fissures and acute mucosal abrasions from stiff or improperly lubricated enema nozzles. Mandatory reporting: Any adverse reaction resulting in hospitalization, prolonged disability, or systemic toxicity must be documented on the standardized National Pharmacovigilance Suspected ADR Reporting Form within 24 hours of stabilization.

section_heading: Section 3: Antidote and Decontamination Protocols for Herbomineral Panchakarma Drugs
text: Toxicological management and decontamination protocols for Panchakarma medications: 1. Vatsanabha (Aconitum ferox) poisoning from unpurified formulations: Symptoms include perioral paresthesia, ventricular arrhythmias, and collapse. Management: Gastric lavage with activated charcoal or tannin-rich decoctions; administration of Tankana Bhasma (borax) mixed with ghee and honey as classical physiological antidote. 2. Bhallataka (Semecarpus anacardium) dermatitis: Severe blistering, edema, and burning erythema. Treatment: Immediate washing with coconut oil or milk; topical application of Coriander leaf pulp (Kothmir) or Tilataila mixed with Shatadhouta Ghrita. 3. Jayapala (Croton tiglium) hyper-purgation toxicity: Administer lemon juice (Nimbu Swarasa) with cold water and butter to neutralize croton resin toxicity.
